method:
ORDER OF JUDGEMENT. The Han calendar parts are attested; the text-grading part is a modern construction, labelled EXPERIMENTAL everywhere it appears. 1. PERIOD HEXAGRAM (calendar, attested): gua qi hexagram of the instant and sovereign (bi) hexagram of the month (Yi wei Jilan tu, Siku text with Zheng Xuan notes; Xin Tang shu 27A Dayan 'gua yi'). 2. CALENDAR VALENCE (attested, thin, weather-and-omen use, not personal): growing sovereign hexagram = emolument (祿), waning = punishment (刑); four cardinal hexagrams = punishment and arms. Jing Fang's own use (Han shu 75) was to test the ruling hexagram against wind, rain, cold and warmth for court omens; no personal topics are attested. 3. LINE: Han gua qi assigns whole hexagrams to days, not lines; Dayan assigns one line per solar term to the four cardinal hexagrams only (an inference from one sentence); line-per-day for the sixty is a modern reconstruction. 4. TEXT GRADE (modern construction): the Chinese judgment (guaci) and assigned line statement (yaoci) graded by the mechanical token table (tables.tokens). Ordering anchor Xici shang ch.3: 吉凶 = gain and loss; 悔吝 = small flaw; 无咎 = good at repairing a fault. Fine ranking is the engine's convention. 5. TOPIC only where the text names it (cue rules); everything else 'general'. 6. MODIFIERS: the position prior and the 貞 condition are held back (unverified).

ENGINE RULES: this tradition has NO natal promise and is not agreement-bearing evidence for wealth. A cue rule emits EITHER the clause's own direction OR the statement-level grade for that topic, never both (the 利 inside a cue clause is already counted by the grader). Each cue clause is graded on its own, never by the whole statement (statement 6.0 grades -3 by 終凶 while its audience clause is favourable). The same hexagram feeds zhouyi.period-hexagram-judgment, zhouyi.line-of-day-reconstruction and dayan.cardinal-line-by-term: they share dedupeKey hexagram@period and count once for the span; if sovereign S equals gua qi H the text is reported once. Statement text rules require the corpus to be re-graded after the token additions; the '17% (76 of 450) have no verdict word' figure of the first reading was overstated by missing tokens and must be recomputed.

topicDefinitions.definition: The Zhouyi's verdict terms (ji, xiong, hui, lin, jiu, li, bu li) are unspecific: they say whether the matter divined turns out well or badly, not which life domain. All 450 statements can carry a general grade; a share carry no verdict word (the share is to be recomputed after the token fixes).
topicDefinitions.significators: The period hexagram (gua qi, or the monthly sovereign hexagram), its judgment, and the assigned line. The Han calendar use (Jing Fang) is about weather and court omens, not persons.
topicDefinitions.source: Zhouyi text via zh.wikisource.org 周易/* (opened, all 64 pages); Han shu 75 (opened)

topicDefinitions.definition: Office and standing, only where the text says so: audience with a superior (利見大人, 7 statements: 1.2, 1.5, 6.0, 39.0, 39.6, 45.0, 57.0), service of a king or appointment of lords (王用, 利建侯, 王事 and similar, about 12 statements), plus the Yi wei rule that a growing sovereign hexagram governs 'emolument' (祿), meaning stipend and standing at calendar level, not wealth.
topicDefinitions.significators: Statements containing 利見大人, 王用, 利建侯, 王事, 王命; sovereign hexagram in its growing half.
topicDefinitions.source: Zhouyi text (opened); Yi wei Jilan tu (opened)

topicDefinitions.definition: Marriage and union only: 取女吉 (31.0), 勿用取女 (4.3, 44.0), 女歸吉 (53.0), 婚媾 (3.2, 3.4, 22.4, 38.6, 51.6), 婦貞 (9.6), plus 納婦 4.2, 老夫得其女妻 28.2, 老婦得其士夫 28.5, 婦人吉夫子凶 32.5, 夫征不復婦孕不育 53.3, 婦三歲不孕 53.5, 婦喪其茀 63.2, each with its own sign. No friendship, family or partnership vocabulary beyond that. No statement is mapped by hexagram name (not 咸, not 歸妹).
topicDefinitions.significators: Statements containing 取女, 女歸, 婚媾, 婦貞, 女壯, 納婦 and the listed spouse phrases.

topicDefinitions.definition: Illness only where named with 疾 or 勿藥. Certain own-illness cues: 25.5, 41.4, 33.3, 16.5. Ambiguous: 24.0, 55.2, 58.4. Excluded unless the director accepts the caveat: 36.3 (不可疾貞 'do not be hasty') and 50.2 (the enemy's trouble). No body-wide or longevity forecast in the text.
topicDefinitions.significators: Statements containing 疾 or 勿藥.

topicDefinitions.definition: Almost unattested. Nine statements name goods or retainers: 56.4 得其資斧, 57.6 喪其資斧, 56.6 喪牛, 34.5 喪羊, 51.2 億喪貝, 56.2 懷其資，得僮僕, 56.3 喪其童僕, and 9.5 富以其鄰 and 11.4 不富以其鄰 whose direction is contested. 利 alone is NOT wealth. The Yijing calendar has almost nothing on money and is not agreement-bearing for wealth.
topicDefinitions.significators: Statements containing 資斧, 資, 童僕, 貝 (loss), 喪牛, 喪羊, 富以.

topicDefinitions.definition: No statement names study or learning as a topic. Do not map any statement to learning.

Journeys and crossings named in the text: 利涉大川 and 用涉大川 (positive, 10 statements: 5.0, 13.0, 15.1, 18.0, 26.0, 27.6, 42.0, 59.0, 61.0, 64.3), 不利涉大川 and 不可涉大川 (negative, 2: 6.0, 27.5), 利有攸往 (13 statements, a general go-ahead) versus 不利/勿用有攸往 (4: 3.0, 23.0, 25.0, 33.1), the traveller hexagram 56, 行人. Home is not a Zhouyi topic apart from 家人 (hexagram 37, not mapped).
topicDefinitions.significators: Statements containing 涉大川, 有攸往, 旅, 行人.

tokens.note: Engine convention, ordinal v. Match on punctuation-stripped text, longest first, left to right, no overlaps. Counts are the pre-correction counts over the 450 statements; re-run after the additions below.
tokens.+1.5: 无不利 (13), 有慶 (added in checking)
tokens.+1: 亨 (34), 小亨 (2), 利 (88; any 利 incl. 利貞, 利涉大川, 利見大人, 利有攸往, 利用), 初吉 (1; void if 終亂 follows), 有喜 (added), 譽 (added), 福 (added, e.g. 受其福), 有終 (added)
tokens.-0.5: 悔 (6), 有悔 (4); 厲无咎 as a pair = -0.5 in total
tokens.-1: 吝 (16), 貞吝 (4), 勿用 (11; 'do not act yet', an engine convention, not misfortune), 无攸利 (10), 終吝 (added)
tokens.-1.5: 厲 (19), 貞厲 (8), 不利 (8), 咎 (4; only where not preceded by 无 or 何), 不可涉大川 (added)
tokens.-2: 災 or 眚 (11), 終亂 (added)
tokens.finalOutcomeOverride: If 終吉, 終凶, 終亂, 終吝 or 有終 occurs, grade = its value (final outcome overrides earlier tokens, including 初吉); flag 'mixed' if an earlier token had the opposite sign. Examples the second reading found wrong before the fix: 63.0 graded +2 (ends 終亂), 37.3 graded positive (ends 終吝), 27.5 graded +2 (ignores 不可涉大川), 25.5 无妄之疾，勿藥有喜 graded 0 (有喜 untokenised), 56.4 graded 0.
tokens.formula: No token -> 0. Else grade = P + 0.5*(sum(v) - P), P the v of largest absolute value, clipped to [-3,+3]; 厲 directly followed by 无咎: 厲 = -0.5 and 无咎 = 0. Flags: 'mixed' if some v >= +1 and some v <= -1; 'conditional' if 貞 sits beside a verdict.
tokens.ranking: 元吉/大吉 > 吉/貞吉/終吉 > 无不利 > 亨, 利 > 无咎, 悔亡 > (no token) > 悔 > 吝 > 勿用, 无攸利 > 厲, 不利, 咎 > 災眚 > 凶. Four-virtue reading of 元亨利貞 versus the two-term reading (Zhu Xi per Legge) is a school difference; the grade is the same.

tables.hanCalendarConstants: 80 parts = 1 day. Standard hexagram 6 d 7 parts = 6.0875 d; 60 x 6.0875 = 365.25 d. Jing Fang as reported by Dayan: kan, zhen, li, dui 73/80 d each (3.65 d total), 頤 晉 井 大畜 5 d 14 parts each, the other 56 hexagrams 6 d 7 parts; sum 365.25 d (arithmetic checked: 487-73 = 414 parts = 5 d 14 parts). The Yi wei note itself also gives the four cardinal hexagrams (四時卦) 73 parts (消息六日七分，四時卦七十三分): the first reading's claim that the Yi wei scheme gives them no days was wrong. Dayan: 冬至初，中孚用事 (中孚 is the first of the sixty at the solstice); 七日來復 in 復 (24.0). Twelve sovereign hexagram names with months and the growing/waning split are the standard Han list but were NOT seen verbatim in an opened text: held back as a table; the engine's own sovereign-hexagram table must be used and a golden test must confirm the split. Whether the sovereign changes at the jie or the zhongqi term is undecided and must be a named convention.

topicCueIds.litigationAndWar: mapped to 'general' only; no cue rule

tables.sources: Chinese text: zh.wikisource.org 周易/{name} raw wikitext, 64 sub-pages = 64 judgments + 384 lines + 用九 + 用六 = 450 statements, received (Wang Bi) text, proofreading level 50%; the 周易 index page carries {{PD-old}} but no licence tag was seen on the sub-pages, so embed only the bare statement characters with punctuation stripped and record URL and fetch date. Known parse defects (hexagrams 10, 12, 13 names inside the judgment, 坤 judgment over three lines, editorial punctuation splitting phrases such as 不利。有攸往 in 23, {{另|A|B}} variants, -{X}- converter markers) are handled in the reference parser. Legge 1882 (SBE 16) on en.wikisource is public domain by age but only 30 of 64 pages were fetched cleanly and no host licence statement was seen: not used in rules. Modern translators (Rutt, Shaughnessy, Hatcher, Kunst) are not quoted.

rules.name: Mechanical grade of a hexagram or line statement (EXPERIMENTAL)
rules.condition: Input: the Chinese statement text (guaci or yaoci). 1) Delete punctuation and spaces. 2) Scan left to right, longest match first, with tables.tokens (including the additions 有喜, 有慶, 譽, 福, 有終, 終亂, 終吝, 不可涉大川); each match gives v in [-3,+3]. 3) No match -> grade 0 with flag 'none'. 4) If a final-outcome token (終吉, 終凶, 終亂, 終吝, 有終) occurs, grade = its value (overriding earlier tokens, 初吉 included); flag 'mixed' if an earlier token had the opposite sign. 5) Else if 厲 or 貞厲 is directly followed by 无咎, 厲 = -0.5 and 无咎 = 0. 6) Else grade = P + 0.5*(sum(v) - P), clipped. 7) 'mixed' if some v >= +1 and some v <= -1; else pos/neg/neutral. 8) 'conditional' flag for 貞吉, 貞凶, 貞厲, 貞吝, 利貞. 勿用 is advice not to act yet (engine convention); 不可貞 and 不可疾貞 are advice, not graded. Always labelled a modern convention.
rules.template: The {kind} of hexagram {hexName} reads '{text}', graded {grade} ({flag}) by the verdict words {tokens}.
rules.sourceCitation: Xici zhuan (Great Commentary) shang ch.3 and xia, via zh.wikisource.org 周易/繫辭上 and 繫辭下, opened; verdict-word list tested on all 450 statements of zh.wikisource.org 周易/* (opened). Grading arithmetic is the engine's own convention.
rules.sourceLocator: 繫辭上 第三章; 繫辭下 (chapter containing 三多凶，五多功)
rules.sourceQuote: 吉凶者，言乎其失得也。悔吝者，言乎其小疵也。无咎者，善補過也
rules.variants: Scholars translate 悔/吝/厲/咎 differently; the ordering hui milder than lin milder than li or jiu is the engine's convention. Whether 貞 means 'divination' (Zhou-era sense, Shaughnessy and Rutt, not opened) or 'correct and firm' (Xici, Legge) changes the reading of 貞吉 but not its grade. Wing commentaries are NOT graded. The second reading did not open Xici; the Xici wording is the standard text.
rules.verificationNote: Missing verdict tokens added; final-outcome override extended; negator and advice handling added.

rules.name: Judgment of the gua qi hexagram of the period (EXPERIMENTAL)
rules.condition: Let H = gua qi hexagram at t and S = sovereign hexagram of the month. Report grade(guaci(H)) and grade(guaci(S)) from zhouyi.statement-grade; when H equals S report one reading, not two. Present as 'the hexagram that rules this period says ...'. Never as a prediction about a person: no source attests applying the judgment text of the day's hexagram to personal outcomes (Dayan: Jing Fang used the hexagrams only to forecast calamity, good and ill, 止於占災眚與吉凶善敗之事).
rules.template: From {start} to {end} the gua qi hexagram is {hexName}; its judgment is graded {grade} ({flag}).
rules.sourceCitation: Yi wei Jilan tu (Siku quanshu text with Zheng Xuan commentary, via zh.wikisource.org '易緯稽覽圖 (四庫全書本)', opened); Xin Tang shu 27A 'Dayan li yi, gua yi' (zh.wikisource.org, opened)
rules.sourceLocator: 稽覽圖 卷下; 新唐書 卷二十七上 曆志 卦議
rules.sourceQuote: 八十分為一日之七者一卦六日七分也
rules.variants: The quoted phrase sits inside Zheng Xuan's note, not the main text, and the Qing editors' warning (卷中錯簡頗多, misplaced slips) is attached to that very passage. Schemes differ: Meng Xi/Yi wei 60 hexagrams x 6 7/80 d; Jing Fang (as reported by Dayan) 73/80 d for the cardinal four and 5 d 14 parts for 頤晉井大畜; the Tianbao calendar ran lines in order.
rules.verificationNote: Quote attributed to Zheng Xuan's note with the slips caveat; cardinal-days claim dropped; H = S counted once.

rules.name: Line of the gua qi hexagram by equal slices (modern reconstruction, EXPERIMENTAL)
rules.condition: Let H occupy [t0, t1) in the engine. line = 1 + floor(6*(t - t0)/(t1 - t0)), counting 1 (bottom) to 6. Report grade(yaoci(H, line)). Always label 'reconstruction: no source assigns lines to days within the 60-hexagram scheme'. Not used for the four cardinal hexagrams (use dayan.cardinal-line-by-term). Not counted as separate evidence from zhouyi.period-hexagram-judgment for the same period.
rules.template: On {date} the equal-slice line of {hexName} is line {line}: '{text}' (graded {grade}). Modern reconstruction, not a Han assignment.
rules.sourceCitation: Xin Tang shu 27A Dayan 'gua yi' (opened): reports Lang Yi's hexagrams all 6 d 7 parts and 'not by successive lines', and the Tianbao calendar's line-after-line method as an error
rules.sourceLocator: 新唐書 卷二十七上 曆志 卦議
rules.sourceQuote: 按郎顗所傳卦皆六日七分不以初爻相次用事
rules.variants: Attested: Han calendars did NOT run lines day by day; Tianbao li (Qi) did (per Dayan, who rejects it). Equal slicing is the engine's construction.

rules.name: Dayan: lines of kan, zhen, li, dui ruling the 24 solar terms (EXPERIMENTAL inference)
rules.condition: Order the 24 terms from the winter solstice. Terms 1-6 (winter solstice to jingzhe) belong to kan, 7-12 to zhen, 13-18 to li, 19-24 to dui. Within each block term k rules line k (1 = bottom). Report hexagram, line and grade of its yaoci. The term-to-line list is an INFERENCE from one sentence, not a quoted table; label it so. Strength lowered to 1 because it only activates a line statement and carries no verdict of its own.
rules.sourceCitation: Xin Tang shu 27A, Dayan calendar 'gua yi' (Yi Xing, 8th c.), zh.wikisource.org 唐書 (四庫全書本) 卷二十七上, opened
rules.sourceLocator: 卷二十七上 歷志 大衍曆議 卦議
rules.sourceQuote: 坎震離兑二十四氣次主一爻其初則二至二分也
rules.variants: Dayan also says kan runs from the winter solstice and ends in the second month, zhen starts at the spring equinox, li at the summer solstice, and credits the scheme to Meng Xi. Jing Fang's own 24-term list in Jing shi yi zhuan xia is a different, palace-based list and is not reproduced.
rules.verificationNote: Confirmed; strength reduced from 2 to 1 as the second reading advised.

rules.name: Growing sovereign hexagram = emolument, waning = punishment (calendar level, weak)
rules.condition: Let S = the sovereign hexagram of the month (12 bi hexagrams). Growing (xi: fu, lin, tai, da zhuang, guai, qian): favourable, topic career/general. Waning (xiao: gou, dun, pi, guan, bo, kun): unfavourable. The list is the standard Han list taken from the engine's own sovereign-hexagram table; it was not seen verbatim in an opened text, so a golden test must confirm the split. 祿 means the official stipend and standing (祿去公室), not wealth; 刑 means penal or military action in an omen context. Calendar-level, weak, no personal forecast is attested.
rules.template: The sovereign hexagram is {hexName}, a {growing_or_waning} hexagram; the Yi wei assigns {emolument_or_punishment} to such periods.
rules.sourceCitation: Yi wei Jilan tu (Siku text, zh.wikisource.org 易緯稽覽圖 (四庫全書本), opened); Xin Tang shu 27A 卦議 (opened) for the origin of the 12 month hexagrams in Meng Xi
rules.sourceLocator: 稽覽圖 卷中 (passage on xiao xi gua xiao); 新唐書 卷二十七上
rules.sourceQuote: 息卦主祿消卦主刑四時四方主刑兵
rules.variants: Zheng Xuan's note splits the twelve differently, as the yin half (pi through lin, 太陰) and the yang half (tai through dun, 太陽) of the year: a separate candidate valence, not implemented. The Siku editors' notes make the passage partly unreliable.
rules.verificationNote: Strength 2 to 1; meaning of 祿 and 刑 fixed; list status stated.

rules.name: Cardinal hexagrams (kan, zhen, li, dui) govern punishment and arms
rules.condition: If the gua qi hexagram at t is kan, zhen, li or dui, emit this marker. Both the Yi wei note and Dayan's report of Jing Fang give each 73/80 of a day, so the marker fires at most about a day per quarter. 頤, 晉, 井 and 大畜 are the four shortened hexagrams (5 d 14 parts).
rules.template: {hexName}, a cardinal hexagram, rules this instant; the Yi wei assigns the four quarters to punishment and arms.
rules.sourceCitation: Yi wei Jilan tu (Siku text with Zheng Xuan notes), zh.wikisource.org, opened; Xin Tang shu 27A 卦議 (opened) for the 73/80-day Jing Fang figure
rules.sourceLocator: 稽覽圖 卷中; 新唐書 卷二十七上 卦議
rules.variants: Same sentence as yiwei.growing-waning-sovereign: the two share dedupeKey yiwei-sentence and are one piece of evidence, not two.
rules.verificationNote: Variants note fixed: the Yi wei scheme does give the cardinal hexagrams 73 parts.

rules.name: Text names a journey or crossing
rules.condition: Grade the CUE CLAUSE, not the whole statement. Positive crossing (利涉大川, 用涉大川): 5.0, 13.0, 15.1, 18.0, 26.0, 27.6, 42.0, 59.0, 61.0, 64.3 -> favourable. Negative crossing (不利涉大川, 不可涉大川): 6.0, 27.5 -> unfavourable. 利有攸往 (13 statements) is a general go-ahead, tagged home-travel with the note 'undertaking or journey'. Negative going (不利有攸往, 勿用有攸往): 3.0, 23.0, 25.0, 33.1 -> unfavourable. Emit the clause direction OR the statement grade, not both.
rules.template: The statement '{text}' names a journey or crossing and is worded {positive_or_negative}.
rules.sourceCitation: Zhouyi text, zh.wikisource.org 周易/需, 周易/同人, 周易/訟, 周易/復 and others, opened
rules.variants: Legge and later translators read 涉大川 as a literal or figurative 'crossing the great river'; 有攸往 as 'having a place to go'.
rules.verificationNote: Crossing lists corrected (15.1 added, 27.5 added as negative); negative going now four statements (23.0 added).

rules.name: Text names meeting a great man
rules.condition: If the statement contains 利見大人 (1.2, 1.5, 6.0, 39.0, 39.6, 45.0, 57.0) tag topic career, favourable, graded on the clause alone (in 6.0 the whole statement grades -3 by 終凶 while this clause is favourable; keep both and show both). Whether this is 'career' is an interpretation.
rules.template: The statement '{text}' says it is profitable to see the great man (a superior or lord).
rules.sourceCitation: Zhouyi text, zh.wikisource.org 周易/乾 line 2 and line 5, opened
rules.sourceLocator: 乾 九二 and 九五
rules.variants: 大人 may mean a lord or an exemplary person; Legge writes 'the great man' (SBE 16, Hexagram 1).

rules.name: Text names taking a wife or a wedding
rules.condition: Tag topic relationships for the statements in tables.topicCueIds.marriage: 取女吉 (31.0) and 女歸吉 (53.0) favourable; 勿用取女 (4.3, 44.0) unfavourable; every other listed statement (婚媾 3.2, 3.4, 22.4, 38.6, 51.6; 婦貞 9.6; 納婦 4.2; 老夫得其女妻 28.2; 老婦得其士夫 28.5; 婦人吉夫子凶 32.5; 夫征不復婦孕不育 53.3; 婦三歲不孕 53.5; 婦喪其茀 63.2) gets its own clause sign, never a blanket 'marriage' sign (51.6 婚媾有言 is mildly negative). No mapping by hexagram name (not 54, not 咸).
rules.template: The statement '{text}' concerns marriage and is graded {grade}.
rules.sourceCitation: Zhouyi text, zh.wikisource.org 周易/咸 and 周易/姤, opened
rules.variants: 取 is read as 娶 by commentators; 匪寇婚媾 'not robber, but wooer' is the common reading in 3.2, 22.4, 38.6.
rules.verificationNote: Seven spouse statements added; hexagram-54 position made consistent.

rules.name: Text names illness
rules.condition: Tag topic health on 疾 or 勿藥 statements. Certain own-illness cues: 25.5 无妄之疾，勿藥有喜 (grades positive after 有喜 is tokenised), 41.4, 33.3 有疾厲 (negative clause), 16.5 貞疾恆不死 (a lasting illness that does not kill). Ambiguous: 24.0 (无疾 absence of illness in a judgment that is mostly 亨), 55.2, 58.4. Excluded: 36.3 (不可疾貞, 'do not be hasty') and 50.2 (疾 belongs to the enemy 仇) unless the director accepts the caveat in writing. Grade the clause; the output grades are those of the corrected grader, not the first reading's earlier examples.
rules.template: The statement '{text}' mentions illness and is graded {grade}.
rules.sourceCitation: Zhouyi text, zh.wikisource.org 周易/无妄 line 5, 周易/損 line 4, opened
rules.sourceLocator: 无妄 九五; 損 六四
rules.variants: 疾 can also mean 'quickly' or 'to hate'.
rules.verificationNote: Examples replaced; certain, ambiguous and excluded cues separated.

rules.name: Text names goods, livestock, retainers or a traveller's provisions
rules.condition: Tag topic wealth on nine statements: 56.4 gain (得其資斧, but 我心不快), 57.6 loss (喪其資斧，貞凶), 56.6 loss (喪牛，凶), 34.5 loss (喪羊 but 无悔), 51.2 loss (億喪貝, regained in seven days), 56.2 (懷其資，得僮僕貞), 56.3 (喪其童僕), and 9.5 富以其鄰 and 11.4 不富以其鄰, whose direction is contested (ambiguous readings): direction neutral. Say that these nine are all the statements that name goods; the Yijing calendar has almost nothing on money.
rules.template: The statement '{text}' names gain or loss of goods; {grade}.
rules.sourceCitation: Zhouyi text, zh.wikisource.org 周易/旅 and 周易/巽, opened
rules.sourceLocator: 旅 九四; 巽 上九
rules.variants: 資斧 'axe and provisions' versus 'a bronze axe as wealth' is disputed; 貝 is cowrie currency.
rules.verificationNote: 'Only seven' replaced by nine; 9.5 and 11.4 made neutral.
